title: Queueing Echo probe: partial KV warm-chain + shadow replicas
content:
Experiment: Queueing Echo probe — partial KV warm-chain + shadow replicas
Owner: Damien Cruz (notes) — quick scratchpad, rough numbers, ascii charts.
Goal:
- Observe tail amplification when partial KV cache priming happens in a mixed-priority arrival.
- Test whether lightweight shadow replicas (no full model state, just KV mirror) reduce p99 without increasing median by >10%.
Hypothesis:
- If we warm a tiny fraction of the KV trie (prefixes from top-10 prompts) and route a small percentage (5%) of requests to shadow replicas during bursts, p99 should drop by 20–35% while p50 remains within 5%.
Environment:
- Fleet: 6x A100 nodes, same batcher config used for last spike tests.
- Model: rdx-7b-quant (int8 hybrid).
- Sequence lengths: 24 tokens avg, tail to 256.
- Workload generator: custom harness (local harness v0.9.3) with arrival patterns: poisson baseline, then paired microburst (2x 10s bursts separated by 30s).
- Priority lanes: 3 (high, normal, background). High was 20% of traffic during bursts.
- Cache priming: pre-populate KV for top-10 prompts (warm-chain size ~5MB per model instance).
- Shadow replicas: single-threaded lightweight process that mirrors KV fetch; cold path still hits main runtime. Shadow receives 5% of requests during bursts.
Run matrix (summary):
- R1: baseline (no warm, no shadow) 
- R2: warm-chain only
- R3: shadow only (no warm)
- R4: warm + shadow (5%)
- R5: warm + shadow (15%)
Quick raw results (median/p95/p99 in ms, approx):
- R1 baseline: p50=48ms, p95=218ms, p99=712ms
- R2 warm-only: p50=50ms, p95=190ms, p99=540ms
- R3 shadow-only: p50=51ms, p95=210ms, p99=420ms
- R4 warm+shadow(5%): p50=52ms, p95=170ms, p99=290ms
- R5 warm+shadow(15%): p50=58ms, p95=160ms, p99=270ms
Notes on numbers:
- R1 shows large p99 due to cold KV fetches + small GC spikes on some nodes.
- Warm-only reduces p99 substantially but leaves many mid-tail events — probably due to missing prefixes not covered by top-10.
- Shadow-only surprising: p99 reduction but p50 bumped slightly (scheduling overhead on the mirror path).
- Combo gives best tail improvement; higher shadow fraction yields diminishing returns and raises median.

Quick interpretation:
- Best trade-off at 5–10% shadow routing with targeted warm chains sized to top-20 prompts rather than top-10.
- Shadow replicas reduce p99 by absorbing a fraction of cold-miss cost without fully duplicating model state. But they add an OS scheduling + IPC cost that nudges medians up.
Open questions / TODOs:
- How sensitive is the improvement to prompt distribution drift? Need a synthetic sweep where prompt zipf parameter changes from 0.8 -> 1.4.
- What is the steady-state cost delta? RPC overhead on the mirror path looked like ~2.4% higher CPU on infra nodes. Need a cost estimate for Dedicated pricing.
- Can we make shadow path co-locate on same GPU host as a lightweight coroutine (reduce IPC)? Try shared memory queue prototype.
- Investigate whether increasing warm-chain from top-10 -> top-50 yields linear benefit or saturates.
Edge cases observed:
- Node-3 showed repeated 3s spike unrelated to KV (OS-level dmesg shows nvlink transient errors). Marked and excluded from aggregated runs; need to repro without Node-3.
- Background lane occasionally starves when shadow fraction = 15% during burst peak — our fairness scheduler needs softer guarantees.
Notes-to-self (short):
- Re-run R4 with top-20 warm-chain, shadow 8%
- Add prompt-drift sweep (+ config) into harness (JIRA-ENG-4281).
- File perf logs to S3 (prefix: infra/bench/2025-11-08/queue-echo) and attach to PR.
Questions for Maya/Aisha:
- Maya: can we get trace samples for p99 events where KV fallback happened? I want KV key histograms.
- Aisha: try a POC of colocated shadow coroutine in your warmup branch?
Linked quick artifacts:
- PR #632 contains warm-chain bootstrap script and basic shadow dispatcher.
- Slack thread summarized initial run failures, pinned screenshots of graphs.
Final quick conclusion (working):
- Lightweight shadow replicas + small warm-chains appear promising to reduce tail latency by ~50% relative to baseline p99 in these microburst patterns. Trade-off: small median increase and extra infra complexity. Worth prototyping colocated shadow path and prompt-drift sweep before proposing rollout.
